Court No. - 89
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 37373 of 2023

Applicant :- Shahzad Alavi And 2 Others
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another

Counsel for Applicant :- Sanjay Pathak,Chandrajeet Yadav
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Paritosh Sukla
Hon'ble Mrs. Sadhna Rani (Thakur),J.

Heard the learned counsel for the applicants, learned counsel for the opp. party no. 2 and perused
the record.
By moving this application u/s 482 Cr.P.C., the prayer is made to quash the impugned order dated 31.1.2023 and the order of the revisional court dated 16.9.2023.

Vide order dated 31.1.2023, the learned A.C.J.M., Court No. 2, Aligarh accepted the protest petition of the opp. party no. 2 and rejecting the final report, summoned the applicants to face trial under sections 452, 376-D and 120-B I.P.C. and vide order dated 16.9.2023, the revision against the order dated 31.1.2023 was dismissed by the Additional Sessions Judge, Court No. 6, Aligarh.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Court No. 6, Aligarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is argued by the learned counsel for the applicants that regarding the incident dated 18.10.2020 on the basis of an application u/s 156(3) Cr.P.C. dated 28.10.2020 an FIR was lodged on 15.3.2022.
After the investigation in the matter, the final report was submitted.
Against this final report, the protest petition was filed by the complainant.
On this protest, the impugned order dated 31.1.2023 was passed by the court concerned.
In the medical report, no ingredient of rape was found.
Under section 201 the inquiry was done, wherein, after recording the statements of the witnesses, finding the incident to be false, the report was submitted by the Inquiry Officer.

The reason of false implication disclosed in the inquiry report is that the husband of the first informant is a criminal Shahzad Alavi And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19097129/
1 type of person against whom case crime no. 152 of 2018 under section 21/22 of NDPS Act and another case crime no. 182 of 2017 under the same section 21/22 of NDPS Act are pending and to keep watch on the activities of the husband of the complainant, the police searches him and the first informant has a doubt that the applicants do mukhbari of police against her husband and give information to the police about him.

sentences.text:
It is submitted that as per her own version, the first informant,
after the incident, did not go to the police station and just on the basis of suspicion of mukhbari by the applicants, they have been falsely implicated in the present case.
Hence,the prayer is made accordingly.

Learned counsel for the opp. party no. 2 opposed the prayer and submitted that in the statements of the first informant under section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. both, she has supported the prosecution version.
Accused Shahjad Alvi is having criminal history of 6 cases.

He is an Ex-councillor (Parshad)
and because of this only the police did not make a fair inquiry and submitted the said report.
From the perusal of the record, it is found that there is allegation of gang rape against the applicants.
In her statements under sections 161 and 164 CrP.C., the victim has supported the prosecution version.
It is true that in the medical report, nothing incriminating has come against the applicants.
The reason of the same is that the medical was conducted on 25.3.2022 after about 1 and 1/2 years of the incident.
Certainly, the medical examination of the victim cannot be of any help of her.
So far as the inquiry report on the orders of the court is concerned, that report was submitted on the basis of the statements of the witnesses and the accused persons.

Admittedly, the statement of the first informant was not recorded by the Inquiry Officer, though the reason in the report is disclosed that even after receiving the notice, the victim did not appear for the statement.

In the application u/s 156(3) Cr.P.C. itself, it has been mentioned that the victim made a complaint to the Superintendent of Police concerned and after that the Sub Inspector concerned had come to her house but her report was not lodged.

For the offence under section 376-D I.P.C., the statement of the victim is the most important evidence and the victim in her application u/s 156(3) Cr.P.C. on the basis of which the FIR was lodged later on and in her statements u/s 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. has given the intact evidence that all the three accused persons/ applicants committed rape on her.
There is no contradiction in these statements.
The trial court also in both the orders on the basis of the statements of the victim reached at the given conclusion.
On the basis of the evidence on record, I find no illegality or perversity in the orders impugned.
The arguments of the learned counsel for the applicants do not inspire the confidence of the court.
The application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. being devoid of merits is liable to be rejected and is hereby rejected.
